name: Enforce planner context and language preferences
description: `packages/plan-core/src/read-tracking.ts:1-105` currently records a task read as also reading its phase and feature, and only exposes a non-blocking advisory. `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts:4351-4357` and `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts:1368-1375` perform start/resume mutation before returning that advisory. The session context at `pi-adapter/src/index.ts:4774-4776` gives the reverse of the user-required order. The desired contract is a hard, session-local gate requiring the exact target lineage to be read with `full=true` in this order: task, then phase, then feature, before task start/resume or switch can mutate state. Pause/switch/session reset must require a fresh sequence. `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts:1552-1554` also defaults blank chat language to Italian; unset language preferences must fall back to English, while an explicitly chosen content language may seed blank chat language. `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts:1455-1465` and `pi-adapter/src/index.ts:3028-3043` already return phase handoff text in tool content, but harness-level regression coverage must prevent content from being lost behind metadata. Preserve human Web UI lifecycle controls and the core's harness-agnostic domain boundary.

acceptedDecisions.title: Hard-gate ordered full context reads
acceptedDecisions.decision: Agent lifecycle operations must require task_get(full=true) → phase_get(full=true) → feature_get(full=true) for the exact target lineage, in that order, before task_start or task_switch can mutate planner state.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Advisory-only parent-read tracking allowed agents to start work without reading the task, phase, or feature descriptions and even treated a task read as implicitly reading its parents.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Keep this enforcement session-local in harness adapters, invalidate it on session start, pause, and switch, require linked requirements separately, and preserve Web UI access for the human supervisor.
